en: Hetuduka, Saññojanagocchakādi (The Group on Fetters, etc., within the Dyads of Causes)
Dependent on a state that is both a cause and a fetter, there arises a state that is neither a cause nor a fetter, by way of the cause-condition. (Abbreviated.
Three [results] in the case of the cause; ... pe ... three in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is both a cause and a tie, there arises a state that is neither a cause nor a tie, by way of the cause-condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition (*hetu*), there are nine [results] … pe … in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*), there are nine.
Dependent on a root phenomenon that is both a flood (*ogha*) and a root, a phenomenon that is neither a root nor a flood arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
In the case of root condition, there are five … pe … in the case of non-disappearance, there are five.
Dependent on a root-conditioned phenomenon that is both a root and a fetter (*hetu-yoga*), a phenomenon arises that is neither a root nor a fetter, by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under the root-condition there are five [answers]... up to ... under the non-disappearance condition there are five.
Dependent on a root-conditioned phenomenon that is an hindrance (*nīvaraṇa*), a phenomenon arises that is neither a root nor an hindrance, by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition, three; ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, three.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor grasping, there arises a state that is neither-root nor grasping by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
With respect to the root condition, three; ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, three.
